title: One Minute, Sub-One-Watt Photothermal Tumor Ablation Using Porphysomes, Intrinsic Multifunctional Nanovesicles
protocol: Combine 200 mmol pyropheophorbide with 98.7 mg 16:0 lysophosphatidylcholine, 76.3 mg EDC, and 48.7 mg DMAP in 5 ml amylene stabilized chloroform.
Stir the reaction mixture at room temperature under argon for 24 hours.
Evaporate the chloroform using a rotary evaporator with heating to 40 °C under reduced pressure.
Resuspend the pyro-lipid isomer mixture in 1 mM CaCl2, 50 mM Tris (pH 8), 0.5% Triton X-100, and 10% methanol at a concentration of 5 mg/ml.
Add phospholipase A2 from honey bee venom at 0.1 mg/ml concentration to the solution.
Incubate the solution at 37 °C for 24 hours.
Add two volumes of chloroform and 1.25 volumes of methanol to the incubated solution.
Extract the mixture and then remove the solvent using rotary evaporation under reduced pressure at 40 °C.
Resuspend the cleavage product in 1% MeOH in DCM.
Purify the resuspended material over a small diol silica column for the isomerically pure pyro-lipid.
Dissolve pyropheophorbide-lipid in chloroform.
Record the concentration of pyropheophorbide-lipid.
Dissolve PEG-2000-PE in chloroform.
Record the concentration of PEG-2000-PE.
Dissolve cholesterol in chloroform.
Record the concentration of cholesterol.
Prepare a porphysome lipid film with 65 molar % pyrophorbide-lipid, 5 molar % PEG-2000-PE, and 30 molar % cholesterol.
Dry the lipid films under nitrogen gas.
Further dry lipid films under vacuum for 1 hour.
Store lipid films at -20°C under argon.
Add 1 ml of PBS to each lipid film tube.
Freeze the test tube in liquid nitrogen until completely frozen.
Thaw the tube in a 65°C water bath until fully melted.
Vortex the tube three times, each for 10 seconds, with 5-second re-heating intervals between vortexing.
Repeat freeze-thaw cycles five or more times until no large aggregates are observed.
Leave porphysome suspension on ice upon completion of freeze-thaw cycles.
Assemble high pressure extruder with two stacked 100 nm polycarbonate filters.
Connect the thermobarrel extruder to a thermostatted circulator for circulating 65°C water bath.
Connect the extruder system to a nitrogen tank for high-pressure supply.
Transfer the porphysome suspension to the extruder chamber using a 9 inch glass transfer pipette.
Set the pressure between 200 and 300 psig on the nitrogen tank regulator.
Open the valve of the pressure regulator gradually until sufficient flow rate is achieved or reach a maximum of 800 psig (5,440 kPa).
Close the pressure control valve after the first extrusion pass.
Release the pressure by opening the pressure relief valve on the extruder top.
Refill the extruder with freshly extruded porphysome solution.
Repeat the extrusion for at least 10 times to ensure homogeneity of the final solution.
Measure the absorption of a diluted sample in methanol using a UV-Vis spectrometer.
Calculate the concentration of the porphysomes using the extinction coefficient of 97,000 M⁻¹cm⁻¹ at 410 nm for pyropheophorbide-lipid.
Dilute the final porphysome solution in PBS for measurement.
Perform three measurements with 15 runs each using a Malvern Zetasizer ZS90 by dynamic light scattering to determine size distribution.
Determine the fluorescence quenching of porphysome by comparing the fluorescence emission of quenched porphysome (1 mM in PBS) and unquenched porphysome (1 mM in 1% Triton X-100).
Take spectra before and after adding detergent using Spectrofluorometer.
Set the excitation to be 410 nm, and emission wavelength range to be 600-800 nm.
Keep porphysomes solution under argon at 4 °C until future use.
Protect porphysomes from light by aluminum foil.
Culture KB cells in RPMI-1640 (with 10% FBS).
Sustain the cells in a 5% CO2 and moisturized atmosphere at 37 °C.
Harvest KB cells using standard cell culture technique.
Keep the cell suspension (20,000 cells/ml) in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) on ice for short-term storage until time of injection.
Prepare KB xenografts on nude mice.
Purchase nude mice from Charles River Laboratories when they are 20 g, aged 6-7 weeks.
Sterilize all animal handling tools prior to experiments.
Anesthetize mice with 2% isoflurane in oxygen carrier gas.
Inject tumor cells suspended in PBS subcutaneously into the right flank of mice.
Wait until tumors reach a diameter of 4-5 mm and thickness of 2-3 mm before proceeding.
Inject porphysomes containing 750 nmol pyro at 200 μl volume intravenously via tail vein.
Set up laser irradiation equipment in an enclosed safety room.
Wear laser safety goggles during laser irradiation.
Hold the laser fiber and a diffuser by a clamp on a stand.
Set the laser power to low level and turn on the laser.
Adjust the height of the laser fiber to achieve an irradiation area of 9 mm diameter.
Calibrate the laser power to 750 mW (1.18 W/cm2) using a power meter.
Turn off the laser after calibration to prepare animals for treatment.
Anesthetize the animals with 2% isoflurane in 100% oxygen carrier gas through a nose cone.
Confirm that the animal is deeply anesthetized by performing a toe pinch on the hind paws.
Monitor tumor temperature using an infrared thermal camera.
Place the camera close to the tumor and take a pre-PTT image along with a regular white-light image before starting PTT irradiation.
Turn on the laser and increase light power to 750 mW.
Position the tumor in the center of the laser beam.
Start timing the irradiation.
Take the tumor temperature image every 5 seconds for one minute of laser treatment.
Turn off the laser after 1 minute.
Stop the gas supply of 2% isoflurane.
Wait until the animal recovers from anesthesia and return it to its cage.
Keep mice at normothermia animal room under 12:12 hr dark and light cycle according to approved protocols.
Inject Buprenorphine (0.05 mg/kg, subcutaneously twice a day for a week following laser irradiation).
Measure the tumor diameter using calipers every two days.
Take a photo of the tumor every two days.
Calculate the tumor volume using the equation V=π/6 · a · b², where a is the long diameter and b is the short diameter.
Sacrifice animals by placing them in a CO₂ chamber when the tumor's long diameter reaches 10 mm.
Perform cervical dislocation following CO₂ treatment.
